recipes.name: Red Cabbage and Apples
ingredients_raw: 2 tart apples - peeled, cored and sliced

steps.text: Heat oil in a medium saucepan. Add cabbage and onion; cook until wilted. Stir in apples, water, salt, and black pepper; cover and simmer about 25 minutes.
Stir in sugar and vinegar; taste for desired sweet and sour level. Cook 5 to 6 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Red Cabbage and Apples
raw_recipe.description: This is a memorable combination, especially when all warm and bubbly. There 's sugar for sweetness and vinegar for a bit of sour, and lots of cabbage and thinly sliced apples. Makes two generous servings.

review.reviewBody: I was searching for this recipe for a few months, I had made it before in culinary school and loved it sooo much. I made a few changed: I used apple cider vinegar, plus more of it, I also used brown sugar rather than the white. I did however cook the cabbage a little too long, I would have liked a more firm texture and the apples lost their texture as well. Otherwise this is a nice dish, a little different and a pleasant change from corn or green beans!

This recipe is very good because it allows for some simple substitutes and still comes out delicious. What I did differently: sautéed cabbage & onion in 1/2 oil, 1/2 butter. Used 2 very firm pears instead of apples since I didn’t have any. Used only 2tbsp sugar instead of 3, used apple cider vinegar instead of white. I also cooked it for about 10 min less than recommended because I thought pears would break down faster than apples. Turns out the whole dish was well cooked in that time and I probably could’ve shaved 5 more min off. I would recommend checking the texture every 5 min after simmering for 10 to get it to your preferred texture. Will definitely make this again.

great recipe. Wife and I loved it. I used the Food Pro to shred the cabbage. Next time I will cut by hand to give more texture. With the increased surface area/smaller shred size that the Food pro shred gave, I lessened the cooking time by 8 minutes. I used 3 apples, and almost quadrupled the sugar/vinegar measurements. I would be cautious to say that the sugar/vinegar would be this or that since it's a taste preference. I used apple cider vinegar and brown sugar.

Wow this looks really similar to my Moms recipe (she is from Germany). We grew up eating this stuff and all loved it - 5 kids. Differences: Add 1 -2 c. water - Simmer for 2 hours - when it's done at 1 T flour to make a little "sauce" optional. Also She used apple cider vinegar and maybe just one tablespoon of sugar. I make it now all the time with 1 T. Splenda - have a big plateful every day for lunch. Good diet food!

Fantastic! I used brown sugar instead of white sugar. I shredded in my foodprocessor with the slicing blade: 3/4 of a large green cabbage, 1/2 of a very large sweet onion, and 3 small Granny Smiths, cored but unpeeled. Fed 6 adults as a side dish. This one is a keeper.

Great recipe, but I made two small changes! First, I used Red Wine Vinegar instead of White Vinegar and Water. I also used a tsp of Cinnamon. I then combined all the ingredients in the Crockpot and let it simmer all day. It was the perfect side to Pork Schnitzel and Spaetzle!

This is a delicious recipe. Instead of 2 tbsp vegetable oil, I sprayed the bottom of the pot with a liberal amount of cooking spray and sauteed the onions for 5 minutes. Then, I added the cabbage with 1/3 cup vegetable broth. Healthier option with virtually no calories and it came out beautifully! Also, I used 2 tbsp brown sugar instead of 3 tbsp white sugar and 3 tbsp apple cider vinegar instead of 3 tbsp white vinegar. So yummy!

Very similar to the way my Polish grandmother (Babcia) used to make this. Sometimes I throw in applesauce along with the apples. I do find it takes longer to cook down and soften the cabbage then the recipe suggests. I have also thrown in some fried kielbasa when I have some on hand. Yum!

Great recipe! I added a bit of grated fresh ginger, 1/4 cup of raisins and a pinch of allspice. Used brown sugar and apple cider vinegar. Next time I will also use apple juice instead of water as I will be making this one again.
I used 2 honeycrisp apples and apple cider vinegar. I've made this several times, it's equally good hot or cold. I add pepper but no salt.
i made it using apple cider vinegar except i used 2 tbls of vinegar to 4 tbls of sugar and it came out perfect for my taste

I added caraway, 5cloves of garlic , 6tablespoons of vinegar, one half teaspoon of pepper flakes. I put lemon and lime juice on the chop apples and added them before serving, it gave a nice crunchy feeling, very good recipe. Even my wife loved it and she hates cabbage.

This was pretty good. I did use apple cidar vinegar and brown sugar as many suggested. It was a successful way to use up extra red cabbage. I made half the recipe and it was the perfect amount. I would make this again.

This was amazing. I made a side of garlic butter Parmesan egg noodles to go with and it all balanced beautifully. I did take a shortcut and used a jarred red cabbage and apples that I found at Aldi which cut down some on the cook time. Wanting to try the cabbage inspired me to find this recipe. Still added the seasonings to the cabbage. Will definitely keep this one for future meals.
I added extra, raw apples to the cabbage and apple salad after it had cooled. I took it to a potluck and people seemed to like it.
No flavor. I expected something more complex. This tastes like ... fried cabbage. It's nothing like what I've had in restaurants.

Quick and easy to make and tasty. I sautéed one small onion and an apple before adding the red cabbage, etc. Would have used apple sauce but we didn’t have any. Used brown sugar, not white. Did not add caraway seeds. Will definitely make again.
I halved the recipe and used it as a side dish. Husband liked it. Will cook again.
Excellent little recipe. Served it with andouille sausage. Delicious!
